title: Computer components and what they do

spans.alt: Computer components and what they do
spans.caption: Key steps and ideas

spans.text: The motherboard connects the processor, RAM, SSD/HDD, GPU, and ports. It has a CPU socket, RAM and PCIe slots, and M.2/SATA connections. Check socket, memory generation, size, and power compatibility before buying parts.

The CPU executes program instructions; cores handle more work at once, and cache keeps frequently needed data close. RAM is temporary workspace for open apps and clears when power is off. Match the CPU socket and DDR memory type to the motherboard.

An SSD stores files on chips and is usually faster than an HDD; an HDD uses spinning magnetic disks and is sensitive to shock. NVMe may use M.2; SATA SSDs use a SATA connection. A GPU creates display images: integrated graphics may suit daily work, while a discrete GPU helps with games, 3D, and video. It may need extra power and VRAM.

The PSU converts wall power to suitable voltages. Fans and heatsinks move CPU/GPU heat; dust blocks airflow. Ethernet/Wi-Fi connect to networks, USB to peripherals, and HDMI/DisplayPort to displays. Power off and unplug before opening a case; do not attempt repairs you are not trained to do.
